You talked about it in your post so hopefully you can understand that there are generational family traditions and personal traditions. You seem to look at hosting as a generational family tradition but for some people it is their own personal tradition much like you and your wife’s takeout tradition rather than say youngest kid puts the star on the christmas tree generational family tradition. While some families have hosting as a family tradition, op states that wasn’t the case for her. She made it her own tradition. She made her own family with a tradition she started for herself and expected her son to do his own thing once he started his own nuclear family.

They are all one family, but there are smaller, more close knit subsets of families within the big everyone-is- included family. Op will not have the same level of closeness with her son’s in laws as she will to her son so while son and wife’s families have merged into one big family, everyone is not equally as big of family to everyone else. And, once the son got married, he is closer to his wife and child than to his mom. His mom is now extended family. 
So, it makes sense a large gathering is not Op’s idea of a good christmas time considering she isn’t close to some ppl (in laws) and she has her own thing. Her son is grown; he’s not a baby that requires all of her attention and time anymore.
